q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a flatweave cotton durrie or rug?
title: Cotton durrie carbon footprint per m2
short: Weigh the yarn in a square metre, including weaving waste, and multiply by your yarn supplier's per-kg figure. Add dyeing, loom electricity if powered, washing, drying and finishing, then divide the unit's energy by square metres woven.
audience: Durrie and flatweave rug makers, including Panipat and Jaipur units

ul: Cotton or recycled yarn by weight per square metre.
Dyeing at your unit or a job dyer, with its steam fuel.
Handlooms use no electricity; powerlooms and shuttleless looms do.
Washing, drying and fringe or binding work.

p: Report per square metre, since rugs are sold in many sizes. Give the weight per square metre.

example.title: Worked example: durrie unit per square metre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 11,595 / 20,000 = 0.580 kg CO2 per square metre
Add yarn and outsourced dyeing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
